title: A local supply cut that does not starve the neighbours: block fuel transport into one body's path (zero flux) instead of absorbing it
summary: c49's thermals local cut (fuel held at 0 in a strip) killed the strip's caps but also thinned the caps beside it (0.59-0.70x vs 0.81-1.00x fed, my review on seeds 3 and 4), because with fast fuel diffusion an absorbing strip is a sink for its neighbourhood. The rubric's local-ablation option needs the neighbours to keep their supply. A strip whose fuel is frozen at its current value with zero diffusive and advective flux across its edges (or fuel regrowth switched off only inside a disc that moves with the target) would cut one body's supply without draining the others.
experiment: One loop: in 20261027T0024-c49-thermals-controls/world.py add a cut mode where, inside the strip, kF = 0 and the fuel's diffusive and advective fluxes through the strip's edges are set to zero (mask the face fluxes), and rerun cut.py on seeds 0, 1, 3 and 4. Pass if caps in the strip die while the outside count stays within the fed twin's range on every seed.
